correctness.rationale: The standard rhombic dodecahedron has 14 vertices and 24 axial-to-cube edges. Each generic central plane cuts one vertex per edge whose endpoint normal evaluations have opposite signs. Signed coordinate symmetry reduces the count to six crossed edges when ordered normal magnitudes obey the triangle inequalities and eight otherwise. The normal sphere consists of eight equal central spherical triangles with sides pi/3 and angles arccos(1/3), plus 24 corner triangles. Girard excess gives P6=8(3 arccos(1/3)-pi)/(4pi)=6 arccos(1/3)/pi-2 and P8=1-P6. The actual standard-library verifier inspects all facet triples, symmetries and sample normals; independent numerical computation gave P6≈0.35095931218364385. Exceptional great-circle normals are measure zero. Finite symmetry check is backed by the analytic two-chamber case split.
